message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most celebrated U.S. composers—spanning classical, jazz‑influenced, Broadway, and popular genres:

| Composer | Era & Style | Signature Works |
|----------|-------------|------------------|
| **John Philip Sousa** (1858–1932) | “March King” – late Romantic/early 20th‑century band music | *“Stars & Stripes Forever,”* *“Semper Fidelis.”* |
| **Scott Joplin** (1867–1917) | Ragtime pioneer | *“Maple Leaf Rag,”* *“The Entertainer.”* |
| **George Gershwin** (1898–1937) | Jazz‑infused opera & Broadway | *“Rhapsody in Blue,* *“Porgy and Bess.”* |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900–1990) | Modernist composer who captured Americana | *“Appalachian Spring,* *“Fanfare for the Common Man.”* |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918–1990) | Maestro of symphonic, film, and Broadway scores | *“West Side Story,”* *“On the Town.”* |
| **Samuel Barber** (1921–1989) | Contemporary classical with lyrical lyricism | *“Symphony No. 5,”* *“A Song for All Seasons.”* |
| **William Schuman** (1921–2009) | Influential modernist and educator | *“Music for Strings, Percussion, and Celesta.”* |
| **Charles Ives** (1874–1954) | Experimental early 20th‑century avant‑garde | *“Concord Hymn,”* *“Three American Songs.”* |
| **Stephen Sondheim** (1930–2021) | Master of sophisticated musical theatre | *“Into the Woods,”* *“Company.”* |
| **Ludwig van Beethoven** *(not US)* — just kidding! |

These artists have shaped not only concert halls but also radio, movies, television, and everyday listening habits across America. If you’re interested in a particular period or genre, let me know—I’d love to dive deeper!
